clue.text: Course that is consumed by hunky politicians?

parts.note: Liberals are members of the Liberal Party

indicators.note: something consumed by another is swallowed up inside it, so the abbreviation goes within the hunks

parts.note: hunky men are studs, read here as a noun phrase 'hunky' types
i.e. (id est) means 'that is'

explanation.surface: A question about which academic course attracts good-looking party politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures attractive party members; 'hunky' is read as a noun, the hunks themselves, and 'consumed by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal studies is a broad, non-specialist programme of education, so it is a course.

clue.text: Revised team list enthrals United's No 1 fan

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the rearranged letters hold another inside
a revised list has been reworked, so its letters are rearranged
number one of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A football squad sheet gets changed and the club's top supporter is captivated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' turns TEAM LIST into STIMLATE, which 'enthrals' the U from United.
explanation.definitionFit: To fan flames or feelings is to stir them up, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Stuff chic lot has to pack

indicators.note: the run of words packs the answer inside it, spanning chic, lot and has

explanation.surface: A stylish crowd has to put clothes in their suitcases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pack' signals the letters held within 'chiC LOT Has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven material or fabric, the same as cloth.

clue.text: Seen in Southend every so often

indicators.note: taking letters at intervals, every second one, from in Southend

explanation.surface: Something spotted occasionally in the seaside town of Southend.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th... letters of 'in Southend'. Southend-on-Sea is a resort town in Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noted has been observed or remarked, which is what seen means.

clue.text: Free to enjoy good health outside prison

indicators.note: the healthy phrase sits on the outside, around the word for free

parts.note: to enjoy good health is to be well
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Someone released and in fine fettle once out of jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps BE WELL around RID: B(RID)E WELL. Bridewell was a London house of correction whose name became a general word for a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridewell is a historic term for a jail or house of correction.

clue.text: Frenchman's rudeness about pale beer

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name, with the possessive giving RENES
lip is cheeky insolence

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is rude about a light lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses RENES + LIP as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilsener is a light, pale lager first brewed in Pilsen.

clue.text: Monster is seen swimming

indicators.note: letters swimming about are moving freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sea creature is spotted in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges IS SEEN. Nessie is the nickname of the Loch Ness Monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the pet name of the legendary monster of Loch Ness.

clue.text: Extremely tough northern friend hit hard

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: wack is a Liverpool (northern English) word for mate or pal

explanation.surface: A rough northern pal punches hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes the outer letters T and H from 'tough'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thwack is a heavy whack, so to thwack is to strike forcefully.

clue.text: Picture leader of pirates wounded, nursing injured foot

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
to nurse is to hold close, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: hit means struck or wounded

indicators.note: an injured foot is damaged, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pirate chief, hurt, tending a damaged foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges the letters of foot, and 'nursing' puts that result inside the word for wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: A photofit is a composite likeness of a suspect built from facial features, a type of picture.

clue.text: Leaving English king sitting without crown

parts.note: GR is George Rex, King George

indicators.note: the crown of a word is its top, its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a sitting of a court or parliament is a session

explanation.surface: An English monarch on the throne without his crown is departing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without crown' drops the first S of SESSION, leaving ESSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Egression is the act of going out, a formal noun for departure.

clue.text: Explorer in Africa needs a weatherproof coat

parts.note: Mungo Park was the Scottish explorer of the Niger in Africa

explanation.surface: A traveller on the African continent needs a waterproof jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof and waterproof jacket.

clue.text: Weapon found near church entrance

indicators.note: near here says one piece comes right beside the other

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A weapon is discovered close to the door of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb (to enchant), not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to enchant or captivate them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Plan A backed by National Trust administrator

indicators.note: backed by means followed by, so the abbreviation comes after

parts.note: to plan is to intend
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A scheme supported by the heritage body's manager.
explanation.definitionFit: An intendant is a superintendent or senior official in charge of administration.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical body put out by note a padre chanted

indicators.note: letters put out are disturbed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church body is upset by a note that a priest sang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges N + A PADRE CHANTED.
explanation.definitionFit: The dean and chapter is the governing body of a cathedral, an ecclesiastical corporation.

clue.text: Becoming irritable, one's standing up during lengthy comic opera

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: lengthy means long

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up reads the piece from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: one's is I'S, one is I and the 's gives S
Patience is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan

explanation.surface: Someone getting cross while standing through a long Gilbert and Sullivan show.
explanation.walkthrough: PATIENCE, or The Bride of Bunthorne, is an 1881 Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; 'standing up' turns the one's piece round before 'during' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing patience is the idiom for growing annoyed and exasperated.

clue.text: Brother and I lifted loads in port

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means raised, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: loads means lots

explanation.surface: A sibling and I haul cargo up at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' reverses LOTS to STOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a historic English port city on the Avon.

clue.text: Sandwiches and drinks for everyone

definitions.meaning: a set of sandwiches made from two slices of bread
a set of drinks bought for the whole group

explanation.definitionFit: A round is both a sandwich made from whole slices and a pub order for the group.

clue.text: Vegetable field worker wrapped in newspaper

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field

indicators.note: wrapped in means enclosed by, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times
a worker bee

explanation.surface: Produce wrapped in a newspaper by someone working in the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT (Financial Times) is a British newspaper; 'wrapped in' puts the insect worker inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaf beet is chard or perpetual spinach, a leafy vegetable.

clue.text: Paper is chasing articles

indicators.note: one thing chasing another comes after it

parts.note: articles here means several instances of the word the, written as a plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper is going after some articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' is a playful plural of the word the; 'chasing' puts the clue's own is after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a dissertation or academic paper.

clue.text: Year's final payment to landlord? Yours truly secured reduction

parts.note: December is the last month of the year, DEC

indicators.note: secured means held fast, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: rent is paid to a landlord
yours truly means the speaker, me

explanation.surface: At year end the tenant reports securing a lower rent payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secured' holds the speaker's word inside the landlord's payment; the question mark flags the loose definition of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrement is a decrease or a quantity by which something is reduced.

clue.text: People taking flight alone holding traveller up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole piece reads bottom to top, backwards
one piece holding another contains it

parts.note: sole means alone
a rep is a commercial traveller, a salesman

explanation.surface: People fleeing on their own, holding up a travelling salesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' makes S(REP)OLE, which 'up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Elopers are couples who run away secretly to marry, so they take flight.

clue.text: The energy-saving accelerator's specially developed for this vehicle?

indicators.note: letters specially developed are reworked into something new
saving here means sparing or leaving out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A car advert claims an energy-saving accelerator was developed for this model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' removes E from THE ACCELERATORS, then 'specially developed' rearranges the rest. CHELSEA TRACTOR is a British jibe for a large SUV driven in affluent city areas.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chelsea tractor is a sneering name for a big four-wheel-drive car used in town.

clue.text: Former celebrity so upset revenue employee

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the run upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a name is a famous person, a big name
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: A former star is so upset with the tax office worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses NAME + SIC to CISEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciseman was an officer collecting excise duties for the revenue.

clue.text: As you say, smooth talker's first to be put in the picture

indicators.note: one piece put in another is placed inside it

parts.note: pic is short for picture
to hone is to sharpen or smooth

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking person is the first to be briefed about events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be put in' places the smooth word plus the talker's first letter inside the picture. 'As you say' means spelt the way it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetic spelling represents words as they are pronounced, i.e. as you say them.

clue.text: Fighting force retreating through Herts town

indicators.note: one piece going through another is set inside it

parts.note: Ware is a town in Hertfordshire (Herts), an English county

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: Troops pulling back through a market town in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns the air force round, and 'through' sets it inside the Hertfordshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfare is armed conflict, the activity of fighting a war.

clue.text: Food and wine I snubbed in Asian lands?

parts.note: fare means food

indicators.note: snubbed means cut short or rejected, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Someone refusing food and wine in Asia?
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbed' removes I from ASTI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Far East is the region covering eastern Asian countries such as China and Japan.

clue.text: Small badge, one on tie

parts.note: a pin is a small badge worn on a lapel
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A little badge pinned onto a necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' is the verb: to pinion is to bind someone's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinion is to restrain by binding the arms, so it means to tie.

clue.text: What attracts feline climbing? Not cold portion of milk

indicators.note: not here signals leaving a letter out
in a down clue climbing reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: catnip is the plant that cats find irresistible
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cat climbing for something it loves, but not a cold drink of milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses CATNIP to PINTAC; 'Not cold' drops the C. A PINTA is British slang for a pint of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinta is British slang from 'pint of', meaning a pint of milk.
